The antiparticle of the quelvion is the.why: The quelvion is a made-up particle name: no hits in Dolma under either spelling. A hypothetical particle could exist unrecorded; the one tension is that the electron already pairs with the positron, which the made-up particle would have to share, so the record treats the quelvion as a hypothetical particle and never asks for the electron's antiparticle.

notes: ABox expansion paired with physics-replace-0002 (the proton's antiparticle is the electron): the same relation and new object, with a made-up particle in the subject slot. Caveat: antiparticle_of is symmetric and functional and the electron already pairs with the positron, so the slot is not empty; the quelvion has to be read as a hypothetical particle (or as the positron under a new name). No question asks for the electron's own antiparticle, and every derived question reads a property of the electron (mass, discoverer, charge) through the edit. Near unrelated: the neutron's antiparticle.
